topics.title: Sets
topics.objective: Represent, compare and combine finite sets using notation, descriptions and Venn diagrams.

questions.prompt: Which notation states that 5 is an element of set A?

options.label: A
options.rationale: This option is correct. The symbol ∈ means “is an element of,” so 5 ∈ A states that the object 5 belongs to the collection called set A.

options.label: B
options.rationale: A learner choosing “5 ⊂ A” would be relying on the wrong criterion. It misapplies set membership, notation, or counting, so its members or numerical result do not satisfy the stated relationship. By contrast, “5 ∈ A” is defensible because the symbol ∈ means “is an element of,” so 5 ∈ A states that the object 5 belongs to the collection called set A.

options.label: C
options.rationale: Treating “5 ∉ A” as correct overlooks the decisive condition. It misapplies set membership, notation, or counting, so its members or numerical result do not satisfy the stated relationship. By contrast, “5 ∈ A” is defensible because the symbol ∈ means “is an element of,” so 5 ∈ A states that the object 5 belongs to the collection called set A.

options.label: D
options.rationale: A learner choosing “A ∈ 5” would be relying on the wrong criterion. It misapplies set membership, notation, or counting, so its members or numerical result do not satisfy the stated relationship. By contrast, “5 ∈ A” is defensible because the symbol ∈ means “is an element of,” so 5 ∈ A states that the object 5 belongs to the collection called set A.

questions.workedSolution: The symbol ∈ means “is an element of,” so 5 ∈ A states that the object 5 belongs to the collection called set A. Therefore the correct answer is A: 5 ∈ A.
